segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: Two tankers, a shut Riyadh airport, and a record pension loss
bullets: Iran claims two supertankers hit mines; no one confirms
Riyadh airport stays shut past its deadline
Russia's strikes on Ukraine's power grid continue
Super Typhoon Champi passes south of Guam

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Sunday, October eighteenth.
Today: Iran says two supertankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz, the United States says it controls the strait, and the airport in Riyadh is still closed after its deadline passed.
Plus a Russian strike on Ukraine's power grid, a waiver that lets Russian diesel in, South Korea's pension fund posting a record loss, and a super typhoon that just missed Guam. Let's go.

segments.strap: IRAN CLAIMS TWO TANKERS HIT MINES; U.S. SAYS IT CONTROLS STRAIT
segments.headline: Hormuz: two claims, no confirmation

graphic.title: Both sides claim the Strait of Hormuz
bullets: Iran's Guards claim two supertankers hit mines
CENTCOM: strait cleared of mines; hits are projectiles

sources.name: Al Jazeera, both sides claim control

lines.text: Iran's Revolutionary Guard Navy says two supertankers, each carrying about two million barrels, hit naval mines and burned. It says they were on an unauthorized route with their tracking dark. State-run Press TV showed footage. No ship was named.
As of early this morning, no independent maritime authority had confirmed it. The Associated Press says it was unclear when any such incident happened. So that is Iran's claim, and only Iran's claim.

Here is the other side. The head of U.S. Central Command, Admiral Cooper, said on Friday, quote, the Strait of Hormuz is controlled by the United States. He said four hundred ships and one hundred million barrels moved through in a week, and that the blockade costs Iran twenty-five billion dollars.
CENTCOM's standing line is that the strait has been cleared of mines, and that the hits on ships are projectiles. Two governments, two stories about the same water.

What the shipping monitors show: the website hormuz dot now counts about eight crossings a day over the past week, against about eighty-five before the war. Zero gas carriers in seven days. Six hundred forty-five commercial ships sitting still.

The British maritime monitor, U.K.M.T.O., logged two more Friday attacks off Saudi Arabia. An R.P.G. fired from a small boat damaged a tanker, and another vessel was hit by an unknown projectile. Crews were safe. Nobody claimed them.

War-risk insurance for tankers is quoted at six to ten percent of the ship's value. Brent crude settled Friday at one hundred nine dollars and eighty-six cents, touching one hundred ten for the first time since May.

segments.strap: RIYADH AIRPORT STAYS SHUT AS DEADLINE PASSES; HOUTHI FIRE CONTINUES
segments.headline: Saudi Arabia and the Houthis

graphic.title: Riyadh's airport deadline passes in silence
bullets: Notice to airmen expired 9 p.m. Z, no reopening
Airlines out to Oct 20 to 24; Delta to March 2027
Coalition helicopter crashes in Najran; 2 crew dead

sources.name: Jerusalem Post, W.S.J. on Iran and the Houthis
Middle East Eye, F.I.I. goes hybrid

lines.text: King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh stayed closed. The notice that barred flights expired at nine p.m. Greenwich time Saturday. No Saudi aviation authority announced a reopening.

Airlines are not waiting. IndiGo and Akasa are out until October twenty-fourth. Air India's group until the twentieth. Air France-KLM until the end of October. Philippine Airlines until November twenty-ninth. Delta has pushed its Atlanta-Riyadh flight to March.

The fallout is spreading. Reuters reported the Future Investment Initiative conference, October twenty-sixth, will go hybrid. The Saudi International golf event is postponed indefinitely, and the Six Kings Slam tennis event moves to December.

Overnight, Saudi Civil Defense issued air-threat alerts for Riyadh, Abha and Khamis Mushait. The Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted two ballistic missiles over Khamis Mushait and a drone over Riyadh. On Saturday it reported four more drones downed and two launchers destroyed in Saada.

A coalition reconnaissance helicopter crashed in Najran. The coalition says it was a technical malfunction and two crew died. It denies a Houthi claim that an Apache was shot down. Houthi claims of hits on Aramco facilities remain unverified.

In Aden, the B.B.C. reports Houthi missiles hit the presidential palace on Thursday. Five killed, sixteen injured. On Friday, two missiles landed about five hundred meters from a departing passenger plane at the airport. Everyone was safe.

Iran's foreign minister again offered to mediate. Yemen's government rejected it, calling Iran a party to the conflict. The Wall Street Journal, via the Jerusalem Post, reports Iran feeds the Houthis targeting intelligence. That is a press report.

Egypt's president says Cairo will take, quote, any measure to help defend Saudi Arabia if asked. And Greece's defense minister acknowledged for the first time that Greek Patriot batteries sit at Yanbu, guarding Saudi energy sites.

segments.strap: RUSSIA HITS 15+ UKRAINIAN ENERGY SITES; ZELENSKY BLAMES U.S. WAIVER
segments.headline: Russia, Ukraine and the sanctions waiver

graphic.title: A grid under fire and a waiver under fire
bullets: Strike on more than 15 energy sites
Zelensky: U.S. disregards the Graham Act
Waiver stays until U.S. says otherwise

sources.name: Associated Press, bipartisan criticism of waiver

lines.text: Russia hit more than fifteen Ukrainian energy sites in an overnight strike, the Associated Press reports. Ukraine's air force says it intercepted all four cruise missiles and most of three hundred thirty-two drones. Zelensky called it one of the largest strikes on the grid.

The Kyiv Independent counts seven killed and about ninety injured across the Friday and Saturday waves. A second daytime wave Saturday brought one hundred fifty-seven drones and six missiles. Then overnight into Sunday, one ballistic missile and one hundred eighty drones. A woman was killed in Zaporizhzhia.

Now the sanctions. Late Friday, the White House signed an order waiving sanctions and duties under the Lindsey Graham sanctions act. The waiver stays until the President or Secretary of State decides otherwise.

Lawmakers from both parties criticized it. Zelensky said the United States, quote, completely disregarded the act, and called for a sanctions blackout. He also said Ukraine was not told in advance about Washington's diesel deal with Moscow.

The Economist's leader calls the scheme scandalous. By its account, the October ninth deal covers three hundred thousand tons of diesel at once, five hundred thousand in November, a million in December, and up to three million more. A treasury license exempts Russian diesel from sanctions until April seventh, twenty twenty-seven.
Europe is going the other way. The Commission president says the twenty-second sanctions package is, quote, work now, with nothing lifted while the war continues. No contents are published yet.
One caution from the desk. A waiver is not a delivery. Whether any Russian diesel actually reaches a U.S. port is a separate question, and nobody has reported one arriving.

segments.strap: GASOLINE $4.33, DIESEL $6.33; MOODY'S: WAR COSTS HOUSEHOLDS ~$2,000
segments.headline: What the war costs at home

graphic.title: Fuel prices and the household bill
bullets: Moody's: nearly $2,000 per household so far
Energy cost growing about $50 a week

sources.name: Associated Press, inflation and the Iran war

lines.text: The Associated Press reports AAA's Friday averages: four dollars and thirty-three cents a gallon for gasoline, six dollars and thirty-three cents for diesel. Gasoline is forty-five percent above its prewar level, and an October record.

Moody's chief economist estimates the Iran war has cost the average U.S. household nearly two thousand dollars, including eleven hundred in energy. At current prices, the energy part grows by about fifty dollars a week.

Supply is tight on both sides of the oil trade. Ukrainian drones keep hitting Russian refineries. Reuters reports Rosneft's Ryazan refinery shut a primary unit after an October fifteenth attack. Governors confirmed a fire at a plant in Surgut.
Ukraine's General Staff claims two more big Russian plants remain halted. That is Ukraine's claim. Russia's diesel export ban runs through October thirty-first.

segments.strap: INDONESIA STOCKS WORST DAY SINCE 1998; KOREA PENSION RECORD LOSS
segments.headline: Asian markets

graphic.title: Asia's market shocks
bullets: Korea pension: 182.4 trillion won lost in Q3

sources.name: Reuters poll via Yahoo, China GDP

lines.text: Indonesia's main stock index fell eleven point five seven percent Friday, closing at five thousand one hundred eighty-five. That is its worst day since January nineteen ninety-eight. The rupiah broke eighteen thousand to the dollar.

The trigger was M.S.C.I., the index company. It opened a consultation on reclassifying Indonesia, citing opaque shareholding, suspected coordinated trading and weak enforcement. A decision comes before June thirtieth.
Indonesia's own response: a minister said M.S.C.I. moved sooner than expected, and announced a reform meeting. Bloomberg reports traders are betting on a rate hike by the central bank next week.

In South Korea, the national pension fund's domestic holdings fell one hundred eighty-two point four trillion won in the third quarter. That is thirty-five percent, the largest quarterly loss on record. SK Hynix accounts for seventy-four trillion of it, Samsung fifty-seven.
Korea's regulators have announced no stabilization fund, no short-selling ban, and no pension buying plan over the weekend. Friday's two percent rebound seems to be the reason.

Next up: China reports third-quarter growth Monday. A Reuters poll of fifty economists expects four point four percent. And Japan's central bank chief says he can't tolerate inflation rising further above two percent. Markets expect no change at the October meeting.

segments.strap: CHINA DRAFTS AI EXPORT CONTROLS; MICROSOFT MODEL
segments.headline: AI and technology

graphic.title: China and Taiwan move on A.I. exports
bullets: Taiwan: chip shipments to China criminal

sources.name: A.I. Policy Daily, Taiwan minister via Bloomberg
The Verge, sites block A.I. agents

lines.text: China's commerce and science ministries have drafted export controls on forty technologies. Fourteen are prohibited, twenty-six restricted. They cover A.I. model weights for models of two trillion parameters or more, plus biotech and solar.

The Taipei Times names Kimi K3 and Alibaba's Qwen three point eight Max as in scope. Open-source work and overseas use through an A.P.I. are generally excluded. The ministry says it is not aimed at any country. Comments run to November fifteenth, and a temporary registration is already live.

Taiwan's economy minister told Bloomberg that A.I. servers and advanced chips will join the controlled list. Shipments to Chinese buyers would become criminal, not just administrative. The legislative text is not yet verified.

Microsoft says it finished pretraining a model called MAI-Base-2. Two point eight trillion parameters, eighty billion active, on sixteen thousand chips in thirty-eight days. It claims big efficiency gains over DeepSeek's base model. That is Microsoft's claim.

On agent security: India's national cyber agency issued its first advisory treating A.I. agents as an attack surface. Forkast says every Indian breach was reported by the A.I. provider, not the victim. And Tencent says a review found no deliberate targeting after a researcher logged twenty-eight hundred unauthorized attempts on Amap.

Meta removed contract language that looked like it allowed A.I. training on business-site content. Meta says it was only a clarification. And the Verge reports more websites are closing their doors to A.I. agents.

segments.strap: CRYPTO ETFS: $610.7M OUT IN A WEEK; BITCOIN NEAR $81,400
segments.headline: Crypto

graphic.title: A quiet weekend after a week of outflows
bullets: U.S. crypto ETFs: $610.7M net outflows, Oct 12 to 16

lines.text: U.S. crypto funds had six hundred ten point seven million dollars in net outflows from October twelfth to sixteenth, Crypto dot news reports from Farside data. Ether funds led with three hundred twenty million. Bitcoin funds lost two hundred twenty-eight million.

Friday was the last U.S. session. Bitcoin funds lost eighty-two million that day, ether funds about seventy million. Over the weekend, prices barely moved. Bitcoin sits near eighty-one thousand four hundred dollars. Ether is about twenty-four hundred.

In South Korea, Upbit, Bithumb, Coinone and Digital X are ending trading support for Zilliqa. Upbit cited signs of a security incident. Two of them also put twelve smaller coins under review for delisting.

segments.strap: BEND SCHOOL SHOOTING: 3 CHILDREN, TEACHER KILLED; 'NO KINGS' RALLIES
segments.headline: United States

graphic.title: Oregon, rallies, and the midterm stretch
bullets: Bend, Oregon: 3 children and a teacher killed Thursday

sources.name: Associated Press, No Kings and midterms

lines.text: In Bend, Oregon, a special-needs teacher and a student wounded in Thursday's elementary school shooting were still in the hospital Saturday. The attack killed three children and a teacher, the Associated Press reports.

Across the country on Saturday, No Kings rallies were held, with organizers urging early voting before the November third midterms. President Trump held a rally in Highland Heights, Kentucky, for Republican candidates.

And a legal fight in California. The Justice Department warned state officials Friday that processing ballots from people federal agencies identify as likely noncitizens could prompt investigation or prosecution. No court ruling has been reported.

segments.strap: KENYA EBOLA CASES RISE TO SEVEN, INCLUDING THREE HEALTH WORKERS
segments.headline: Health

graphic.title: Ebola in Kenya, cholera in Zambia
bullets: 3 of the new cases are health workers

lines.text: Kenya's Health Ministry confirmed four more Bundibugyo Ebola infections, including three health workers who treated the first patient. The total is seven, with one death. The new patients are isolated and getting care.
The ministry says one hundred twenty-eight of one hundred thirty contacts have been traced, and there is no evidence of spread in the community. No travel or trade limits have been imposed.

The C.D.C.'s latest table, with data through October fifteenth, counts about ninety-two hundred confirmed cases and forty-four hundred deaths, almost all in Congo. It is the second-largest Ebola outbreak on record.
Separately, Zambia reports nine hundred sixty-six cholera cases and twenty-five deaths across twelve districts. A vaccination campaign has started.

segments.strap: SUPER TYPHOON CHAMPI PASSES SOUTH OF GUAM; HURRICANE TRUDY HITS MEXICO
segments.headline: Weather

graphic.title: Storms in the Pacific and floods in Chennai
bullets: Champi: Cat 4, 150 mph, passed south of Guam
Hurricane Trudy: Cat 2, Mexico's Pacific coast
Chennai: 222 mm of rain in 24 hours

sources.name: Guam Pacific Daily News live blog

lines.text: Champi passed ten to twenty-one miles south of Guam early Sunday. The National Weather Service said the island was, quote, definitely spared the worst. On the way out, Champi was upgraded to a super typhoon, with winds of one hundred fifty miles an hour.

Damage so far: high surf, fallen trees, torn roofs on the south side. About half of power feeders are back on. Guam's hospital ran through the storm, and sixteen babies were born. All schools are closed Monday.

Champi is heading west. The Philippine weather agency expects it to enter its area Tuesday as a super typhoon, with the local name Rosal. Models keep it off the Philippines, possibly near Batanes. Taiwan could see impact next weekend. That is a forecast.
On the other coast of the Pacific, Hurricane Trudy hit Mexico's coast as a Category two with a hundred mile an hour winds. A warning stands from Manzanillo to Cabo Corrientes.

In India, Chennai flooded overnight. Ennore Port logged two hundred twenty-two millimeters of rain in twenty-four hours. Fifteen thousand civic workers are deployed, and heavy rain is forecast for seventeen districts.
And in the Philippines, Kanlaon volcano sent up another ash plume Sunday. Alert level two stays, and sulfur dioxide output rose.

segments.strap: KOLKATA PANDAL CRUSH KILLS 19; TRUCK PLOUGHS INTO TEMPLE CROWD
segments.headline: Disasters in South Asia

graphic.title: Deadly crowds in India, a fire in Bangladesh
bullets: Gwalior: truck hits temple devotees, 12 to 15 killed

lines.text: In Kolkata, a crowd crush at a Durga Puja pandal on Saturday evening killed nineteen people and injured twenty-five. Rain and a misleading announcement are blamed. Seven organizers are arrested in a culpable-homicide case.
In Gwalior, a truck loaded with paddy lost control on a steep road around one-thirty a.m. and ran over devotees at the Shitala Mata temple. Twelve to fifteen were killed and twenty-seven hurt.
In Bangladesh, a fire gutted a resort on Inani Beach at Cox's Bazar and killed ten tourists, six of them from one family. The manager is detained.

In Delhi, protests against the chief election commissioner widened. Two activists were released on bail. A farmers' march to Delhi is called for October twenty-third. And six U.S. Democratic lawmakers wrote Secretary of State Rubio about the detentions.

segments.strap: ISRAEL ELECTION POLLS DEADLOCKED; KENYA PROTESTS PLANNED TUESDAY
segments.headline: World politics

graphic.title: Elections and unrest around the world
bullets: Israel votes Oct. 27: blocs tied at 51 to 51
Palestinian killed in Gaza City strike

lines.text: Israel votes October twenty-seventh. Four polls average twenty-one and a half seats for the Yashar party and nineteen for Likud. The two blocs are tied, fifty-one point two five to fifty-one. Neither has a majority.

Bennett and Liberman say they will pass laws against Netanyahu right after the election. And Qatar's news agency reports a Palestinian was killed in an Israeli strike on Gaza City on Saturday despite the ceasefire.
Also, Israeli police opened an investigation into an alleged assault on diplomats visiting Taybeh in the West Bank. Israel's military says the visit was not coordinated and no soldiers were present.
In Kenya, activists say they will hold nationwide protests Tuesday unless the government lowers fuel prices. In Sri Lanka, an island-wide power outage was reported Sunday. The cause was not given.
And New Zealand votes November seventh. Advice to the prime minister shows he passed over two easier dates. Labour says that will suppress turnout. That is Labour's claim.

segments.strap: JAPAN'S MARS MOON PROBE SET FOR LAUNCH TUESDAY
segments.headline: Science and space

lines.text: Japan's space agency plans to launch its Martian Moons eXploration probe Tuesday at four forty-one a.m. Japan time. That is seven forty-one p.m. Monday Greenwich time. An H3 rocket flies from Tanegashima.
The mission carries a rover built by German and French space agencies. Backup dates run from October twenty-first to November seventh. No delay has been reported.

segments.strap: RAYS TIE ALCS 2-2; TEXANS-JAGUARS AT WEMBLEY; DENA SWEEPS
segments.headline: Sports

graphic.title: Playoffs and a game in London
bullets: Texans vs. Jaguars, 9:30 a.m. ET, Wembley
DeNA sweeps Hanshin; Japan Series Oct. 24

lines.text: Tampa Bay beat Cleveland seven to three in Game Four of the American League Championship Series. The series is tied two-two. Game Five is Sunday in Cleveland.

In the N.F.L., Houston plays Jacksonville at Wembley Sunday at nine-thirty a.m. Eastern. The league lists Texans receiver Tank Dell, running back David Montgomery and safety Jalen Pitre out. Jaguars cornerback Montaric Brown is out. The forecast is about fifty-eight degrees and a sixty percent chance of rain.

In Japan, the DeNA BayStars beat Hanshin eight to five and swept the series. They face SoftBank in the Japan Series, starting October twenty-fourth. In cricket, the India–West Indies decider was washed out. The series ended two-two.
And in Korea's baseball playoffs, KIA beat LG five to one in Game One.

segments.strap: ALSO TODAY: MUSK SETTLEMENT, TIKTOK BAN, TESLA CRASH
segments.headline: Also today

graphic.title: Also today
bullets: Musk settles $1 million voter giveaway suits
Tesla driver says he slept on F.S.D.
Fake WhatsApp clone on Google Play

lines.text: The Verge reports Elon Musk settled lawsuits over his one-million-dollar voter giveaway. Terms were not in the headline.

It also reports TikTok banned the account for a documentary about Musk. A Tesla driver told highway patrol he was asleep while using Full Self-Driving when he hit patrol cars. That is the driver's account.

Apple updated App Store rules to target A.I. apps that create fake nude images. A fake WhatsApp clone ranked above the real app in Google Play. And audio from Wu-Tang Clan's one-copy album was played on a podcast.
